chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from Sa'd al-Iskaf said:

We do not know him except that he said: From Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'There was a worshipper among the Children of Israel, and Dawud (peace be upon him) was impressed by him. So Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed to him: "Do not be impressed by anything of his affair, for he is showing off." He said: So the man died, and Dawud (peace be upon him) was brought news, and it was said to him: The man has died. Dawud (peace be upon him) said: Bury your companion.'
He said: 'So the Children of Israel objected and said: How could he not attend him?'

He said: 'So when he was washed, fifty men stood and testified by Allah that they knew nothing of him except good. So when they prayed, another fifty stood and testified by Allah that they knew nothing of him except good. So when they buried him, fifty stood and testified by Allah that they knew nothing of him except good.'
So Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): "What prevented you from testifying for So-and-so?" Dawud said: "That which You revealed to me of his affair."

So Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed: "Indeed it was so, but a group of the Ansar and the monks testified that they knew nothing of him except good, so I accepted their testimony on his behalf and forgave him based on My knowledge of him."

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Helpers / a group known for piety and testimony
key_terms.عِلْمِي فِيهِ: My knowledge of him (divine omniscience regarding his inner state)
key_terms.مُرَاءٍ: Showing off / performing deeds for the sake of being seen by others

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the worshipper among the Children of Israel and Prophet Dawud's reaction to his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia concept of *al-batin* (the inner reality) versus *al-zahir* (outward appearance), highlighting how Prophet Dawud’s reliance on divine revelation (*wahy*) superseded the consensus of the Children of Israel. It underscores that while human testimony is valid for general judgment, Allah’s ultimate forgiveness is based on His complete knowledge of the heart, even for those who practiced *riya'* (showing off) if He wills. This narrative serves as a reminder for scholars and believers to avoid absolute certainty in judging others' sincerity, as only Allah knows the true state of the soul.
